subject: ADR-175: the ordination page's outputs, read -- the dissimilarity matrix byte for byte against the suite's Bray-Curtis port, the coordinates by their shape, the print held
body: TWO EXPORTS, TWO KINDS OF CLAIM. audit_outputs listed ordination next: Copy coordinates, Copy dissimilarity matrix, Print / save PDF, none read. The matrix is the file a reader takes to R, and for the task's last run (the quoted four-site data, square-rooted, Wisconsin-standardised, Bray-Curtis) it is a deterministic function of the data and the settings; verify_ord has carried Python ports of wisconsin() and bray() held against scipy since ADR-149, so the task holds it BYTE FOR BYTE (,X,Y,Z,W; four rows; six decimals; zeros on the diagonal; symmetric -- X-Y 0.189902, X-W 0.101337, Y-Z 0.480846) and the suite recomputes it and holds the task's literal to the port -- one digit changed fails it (skipped, and said so, where numpy is absent). The coordinates are not that kind of number: the export's own last line says NMDS axes are arbitrary and the configuration may be rotated or mirrored and fit equally well; ADR-140 declined to hold the plot's positions for the same reason, and the export gets the same answer -- the task holds site,NMDS1,NMDS2, a row for each of X, Y, Z and W, the warning with stress-1 = 0.0000 and no NaN, and the suite holds that the step pins NO six-decimal number, so a later hand that tightens the task by pasting positions in is caught. Print / save PDF -> exactly one payload, a print; then the parse and the verdict read once more. ordination 0 -> 3 OF 3 OUTPUTS HELD, ceiling 3 -> 0; the kit's unread outputs 12 -> 9 of 66; the task 70 -> 89 confirmed, 0 refuted; verify_ord 111 -> 114. Held: the copy on this page arrives as a copy payload (the page's clipboard path falls through to execCommand under the harness), and the task holds the kind it actually is; the sixth decimal is the page's toFixed(6) and the port formats the same way. No page was edited; seven pages still hand something over unread.
